events.title: The Battle of Lake Poyang begins
events.description: The fleets of Zhu Yuanzhang and Chen Youliang clashed on Lake Poyang in one of the largest naval battles in history. Zhu's victory weeks later opened his path to founding the Ming dynasty.
events.html: The fleets of Zhu Yuanzhang and Chen Youliang clashed on Lake Poyang in one of the largest naval battles in history. Zhu's victory weeks later opened his path to founding the Ming dynasty.

events.title: John Pascoe Fawkner's settlers land at the site of Melbourne
events.description: Settlers sent by John Pascoe Fawkner went ashore on the Yarra River, building the first houses of what became Melbourne. It grew into Australia's second-largest city.
events.html: Settlers sent by John Pascoe Fawkner went ashore on the Yarra River, building the first houses of what became Melbourne. It grew into Australia's second-largest city.

events.title: Ty Cobb makes his major league debut
events.description: Eighteen-year-old Ty Cobb hit a double in his first game for the Detroit Tigers. His lifetime batting average of .366 remains the highest in major league history.
events.html: Eighteen-year-old Ty Cobb hit a double in his first game for the Detroit Tigers. His lifetime batting average of .366 remains the highest in major league history.

events.title: The Washington-Moscow hotline goes into service
events.description: A direct teleprinter link between the White House and the Kremlin began operating. Set up after the Cuban missile crisis, it aimed to prevent war by misunderstanding; it was never a red telephone.

events.title: East Timor votes for independence
events.description: In a UN-run referendum, 78.5 per cent of East Timorese voted for independence from Indonesia. Militia violence followed until an Australian-led force restored order; independence came in 2002.
